entities.summary:
Mircea II of Wallachia (1428–1447) was the Voivode, or prince, of Wallachia in 1442. He was the oldest son of Vlad II Dracul and brother of Vlad Țepeș and Radu cel Frumos. He was the grandson of his namesake Mircea the Elder.

As the ruler of Wallachia, Mircea II played a significant role in the politics of the region during the Late Middle Ages. He attempted to consolidate his power and resist the influence of the Ottoman Empire, but ultimately succumbed to the pressure and was forced to sign the Treaty of Bucharest, which led to the annexation of Wallachia by the Ottoman Empire.

Mircea II's reign also saw significant cultural and economic developments in Wallachia. He encouraged the development of trade and commerce, and his court attracted scholars and artists from across Europe.

Despite his efforts to promote the interests of Wallachia, Mircea II's legacy was ultimately overshadowed by the rise of the Ottoman Empire, which would go on to dominate the region for centuries.

Mircea II's life and reign serve as a reminder of the complexities and challenges faced by the rulers of medieval Wallachia, and the enduring impact of their decisions on the course of history.
